newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel rises after rare cargo trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel rises after rare cargo trade.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil kicked upwards on Friday, defying the weakness in crude and other oil products, on the back of rare cargo business.

A trader bought 25,000 tonnes from Coryton in the U.K. for delivery to Portugal at a robust $80 fob. Good demand and poor supply in the Mediterranean, where end-user buy tenders have been issued this week, helped bolster values.
The trade, in an illiquid market, pushed prices up on the bid side by $4 to $5, and supported higher bids in the Med, which were heard around the $83 to $84 level.
Earlier high sulphur barges slid $1 in very thin business. But with bunker prices in northern Europe at a world low business in the shipping market is expected to be brisk next week.
Low sulphur prices, by contrast, were in the doldrums, with the market talking deals around $90 to $91 fob NWE, but no business seen done.
Traders said the slide in crude and a healthy supply, particularly in the second half of April, was weighing on low sulphur, which in turn would cap the high sulphur rise.
